result.title: R-BED: A Consequence-Aware Framework for System-Level AI Evaluation and Continuous Assurance
result.comment: 22 pages (18 pages main text plus appendices), 8 figures, 11 tables. Specification-level methodology with a synthetic walkthrough; no empirical validation. Companion reproducibility script available from the author
result.summary: Evaluations of AI systems usually report properties of a model, while decisions to deploy concern a configured system: a model together with prompts, tools, permissions, data, safeguards and an operating context. We ask how evidence about technical failures, deployment-control effectiveness and real-world consequences can be connected to defensible authorization decisions throughout the lifecycle of a deployed system. We present R-BED (Risk-Based Evaluability Design), a specification-level methodology with a fixed 6+4+3 architecture of thirteen diagnostic dimensions (technical failure, deployment controls, consequence and impact); a failure-mediated expected-loss identity that is kept separate from intended-behavior and misuse pathways; bounded evidence statuses with independence levels; a control assurance ladder; five authorization dispositions governed by eight rules; and a Continuous System Evaluation (CSE) layer in which evidence carries a configuration pin, an expiry and declared dependencies, so that a change invalidates evidence in proportion rather than wholesale. We work through a synthetic refund-agent walkthrough, with a deterministic script that reproduces every number, to show how a task-success view can miss a consequential control weakness that the procedure identifies as missing evidence. The contribution is a reproducible methodological specification. Most components are standard practice integrated into one evidence-to-decision record; the Evidence Validity Register, the authority envelope and the tier rules are proposals. None has been empirically validated, and we state seven hypotheses for independent testing.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 R-BED 规范级框架，用固定的诊断维度、期望损失恒等式、证据状态与授权规则把技术失败、部署控制与真实后果证据串成可复现的授权决策记录，并以合成退款代理走查演示。
AI.relevance_reason: 其证据状态分级、过期与依赖触发的按比例失效，以及证据到处置的规则化决策，可能为 LVR 中「视觉证据是否充分、何时停止获取或需重新验证」的评价与记录方式提供线索，但无多模态实验，需核查其可迁移性。
